evidence.quote: purchasing longer-term Treasury securities, initially at a pace of $45 billion per month, following the completion of the maturity extension program at the end of the year.

the Committee expects that a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy will remain appropriate for a considerable time after the asset purchase program ends and the economic recovery strengthens.
Furthermore, strains in global financial markets continued to pose significant downside risks to the economic outlook.
Incoming information pointed to stable, low inflation that was running a little below the Committee's longer-run goal of 2 percent.
Several others thought that it would probably be appropriate to slow or to stop purchases well before the end of 2013, citing concerns about financial stability or the size of the balance sheet.
progress in reducing unemployment was expected to be relatively slow.

This is tempered by notable participant concern about the costs of purchases and calls by several to slow or stop purchases well before end-2013.
